name: Washington, D.C.
industries: Federal agencies and the government-contracting corridor make certified project management a contractual necessity.
intro:
Washington's project market is the federal market: agencies executing modernization mandates, the contractor ecosystem from Crystal City to Tysons delivering them, and oversight regimes that make certified project management a contractual requirement rather than a preference. PMP density in the DC metro is the highest in America because contracts demand it; agile credentials surged as federal IT adopted iterative delivery. We run live online cohorts throughout the year on Washington, D.C.-friendly hours — weekend Saturday–Sunday batches and midweek Wednesday–Thursday batches both — meaning learners in Washington, D.C. attend at ordinary local times, never overnight; the table below shows each upcoming date converted for Washington, D.C.. What doesn't change: one weekend of live expert instruction, methodical exam application support, full-length mock exams, and open trainer access until you're certified.

Washington DC is the PMP's historical heartland: federal contracts routinely require certified project management on staffing plans, which makes the credential a billability gate across the govcon ecosystem from the District through Northern Virginia. Agencies' own modernization programs mirror the requirement internally. Training runs live online across two consecutive days shown in DC local time on this page — no Beltway, no leave slip. Cleared-plus-certified professionals command the region's strongest premiums, and the sourced DC entries in the salary table below put current numbers on the certified baseline. The employer list reflects the contractor-agency-nonprofit mix hiring here, and contractors staffing new task orders can certify delivery teams quickly through private cohorts.
